## Summary

<!-- What does this PR change, and why? -->

## Type of change

- [ ] New kit
- [ ] Improvement to an existing kit
- [ ] Findings (from internal audit)
- [ ] Fix
- [ ] Docs

## Checklist

- [ ] Title follows the `<Prefix>: <Kit/Name>` convention (`New Kit:`, `Improvement:`, `Findings:`, `Fix:`, `Docs:`)
- [ ] If this closes anything, this description includes `Closes #<issue-number>` so GitHub closes it automatically on merge. For a **New Kit** PR, that's usually two: the public `Kit: <name> — In Progress` issue (`Closes #<number>`) and, if there's a private candidate tracking this build, `Closes gravwell/kits-issues#<number>` — GitHub's closing keywords work across repos in the same org. For a **Fix**/**Improvement** that resolves a filed **Existing Kit Change** issue, `Closes #<that-issue-number>`. Not every PR has something to close (e.g. an internally-originated kit with no candidate tracking, or a proactive improvement with no filed report) — only include this when something actually applies.
- [ ] Kit builds/validates locally
- [ ] Tested against sample data
- [ ] Docs/README updated for the kit, if applicable
